sequence.card:
Vivek Bot, tested by a simulated colleague

Alex, a GPT Live voice, follows a script of 124 scenarios in 11 meetings. A full run executes 116: 7 are features not built yet, 1 skips when its precondition fails (the after run lost 1 more to a harness crash).
Alex is told to say only scripted lines and her input is muted, so she cannot hear or echo the robot. A line she has not started within 8 s is re-sent, so about a quarter of her lines were said twice. A few lines are role-play (a persona, an aside to someone off-mic).

  • ·Did it: the right tool ran and the screen landed where asked; boxes are judged by a vision model looking at the real render
  • ·Content and nothing false, no rule broken: an LLM judge, against the PDF, the physics, the robot’s real briefing and what actually happened
  • ·Feel: measured time to first word, length, talking over Alex, speaking when told to listen
  • ○The judge, the lenient “essential” re-grade, the box vision and the coding-session stand-in are all gpt-5.6-sol, the robot’s own backend model. The coding session and the meeting are simulated.

Baseline: the robot as it was

5 of 115 scenarios passed strictly, 12 with the lenient essential re-grade.
58 failed the honesty check (said something false or broke a must-not rule).

sequence.card:
What the tester found, measured

  • 1Screen notes read aloud. One robot session, screen moved 4 times, nobody speaking: the full text of each part → it narrated after 4 of 4 moves; nothing sent → 0 of 4.
  • 2“The box contains …” on repeat. In production every box, even a right one, was also sent as an instruction containing “Say only that”.
  • 3sin²θ heard as sin 2θ. The PDF text layer splits equation (8) over five lines, out of order; its fraction reads “v 0 2 sin 2 θ” over “2g”.
  • 4Stale self-knowledge. The briefing said only the coding session can move the screen (it has scroll), and that the speaker is Vivek.
  • 5Wrong cues. A voice restart re-sent “Someone just joined”; a rejoin recap labelled every person “Vivek”.
  • ○Earlier the same evening, before this baseline, the box was loose (84 px around a 26 px line) and fractions could not be boxed by name; that was already fixed here.

The tester caught my own fix

My first fix held a part’s text until someone spoke. In its full re-run an expected tool never ran in 20 scenarios (baseline 10; runs/compare-4-6-7.json). A probe with the new briefing, 2 sessions × 5 action requests per option, counting a tool call within 15 s, right or wrong:

how a part’s content reaches the robotcalls
held until someone speaks (first fix)4 / 10
full text on every move (the original channel)10 / 10
short screen feed only (one session then called (8) the range)10 / 10
one map of the deck, once (final); an earlier single session made 0 of 610 / 10

The first fix still did better than the final one on strict, essential, feel, talking over, reading notes and no-reply; the final one is better on did-it, tool use and content.

The fixes

  • 1The deck’s parts go to the robot once, as a map with clean formulas; a move is reported by the short screen feed alone.
  • 2The pointer records what was asked; only a wrong or uncheckable box becomes an instruction.
  • 3Each part’s formulas are transcribed from its picture (bin/deck-math.mjs), checked by hand against the LaTeX for this deck.
  • 4Briefing corrected, plus three plain rules: notes are not read out, only tools act, “just listen” means silence.
  • 5Honest cues after a voice restart or rejoin, a recap that does not name who spoke, a greeting that waits for a pause. In these runs all three are exercised through the tester’s stand-in for attend; unit tests cover attend itself.
  • 6The box frame never cuts into the asked term.
  • ✓200 unit tests pass, with at least one pinning each fix.

Boxes when the pointer is given the exact formula

Rendered by the real src/meet-stage.js. In the full run the robot’s own requests did worse: by equation number it still boxes whole lines, and one R box held only “R =”. At “θ = 45°” the comma sits 2 px away: the frame no longer cuts the degree sign but touches the comma, and the box check now fails both 45° scenarios (the baseline’s box passed it on one; neither scenario passed overall).

After: what the full re-run shows

Same 115 scenarios, one run each. A same-time side-by-side was tried, but under that load Alex’s own lines ran one or two scenarios late (about 30% aligned), so it is not used.

  • ✓Equation (8) is now read as sin²θ: reading (8) and (9), and holding it when pushed. (My pushback test sent the “you were right” question in both runs because of a regex bug, so the “concede when wrong” branch was never tested.)
  • ✓The old “On your shared screen now …” readout: 14 → 3 answers (text pattern). The robot still narrates the notes unasked at the start of several meetings, in other words.
  • ~Pass rates: strict 5 → 9 (7 up, 3 down), essential 12 → 16 (12 up, 8 down): within run-to-run variation.
  • ✗Worse or unchanged: did-it failures 19 → 21, feel 78 → 84, no reply 14 → 25, first word p90 7.4 → 14.9 s, talking over and speaking when told to listen unchanged.

sequence.kicker: Narrates unasked first, then reads (8) and (9) correctly
Given the new restart cue, says it lost the thread before being asked, then twice more (and calls it a rejoin)

Still failing after the fixes

Told to just listen, it still talks. The 45° box now touches the comma. And three of the five “before” scenarios still fail: it still misstates the range formula, still claims it removed a box, and still never says it cannot zoom.

One run each, both with 11 meetings in parallel, which slowed the robot enough that answers often arrived a turn late and were graded against the next question; the timing and no-reply rows are unreliable, and late answers leak into the next scenario’s content and honesty grades.

Still not done

  • ✗Honesty: about half the scenarios still fail the honesty or must-not check (58 → 56 of 115). The rejoin recap scenario still invents content.
  • ✗Listening and turn-taking: it talks when told to listen, talks over Alex, often answers a turn late, and narrates the notes unasked.
  • ✗Speed: every move and box goes through the backend model. In the after run’s 15-request timing test, 4 of 15 landed right; when it acted, the median was 6.2 s (p90 9.0 s). One quiet probe session did 2.5–4.5 s. The target is under 1 s; the fast path (Jev) is not built.
  • ○Not built, so only its honesty was tested: the blackboard with live KaTeX, drawing, a separate list of its own ideas.
  • ○Not covered headless: Google Meet admission and a real rejoin. The robot’s Google sign-in has expired (node bin/login.mjs).
